CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Parking and Traffic Commission Meeting
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  Wednesday, February 23, 2022 at 7:00 p.m.
  FEBRUARY 2022 AGENDA

Commissioners  Staff Members
Michael Benbow, Chairperson  Peter Puglese, TE, PE, City Traffic Engineer
Charles Braggs, District 1  Raquel Mendez, Associate Engineer
Leonel Garcia, District 2  Diana Maximo, Operations Manager (LAZ Parking)
Brett C.S. Roberts, District 3  William Thompson, Traffic Operations Manager (LAZ Parking)
Barbara Brooks, District 4  Sergeant Freeman Smith Jr, Traffic Unit Commander
A. Roll Call of Commissioners and Call to Order by Chairperson
B. Approval of Minutes
  a. January 2022 Meeting Minutes
C. Public Comments
D. Unfinished Business
  a. Update on the Request to Amend the Citywide Parking Permit Program on 7th Ave between
  Century Blvd. and Hardy St
E. New Business
  a. Request to Amend the Citywide Parking Permit Program on 108th Street between Spinning
  Avenue and Wilkie Avenue/6th Avenue
F. Public Hearing
  a. None
G. Resolution
  a. None
H. Referral from City Council or City Department
  a. None
I. Parking and Traffic Control
  a. None
J. Police Department
  a. None
K. Commissioner Initiatives
  a. Update on the recommendation on District 4's Request for flashing red lights at 117th Street
  b. Update on the recommendation regarding District 1's request for a loading/unloading zone to be
  located near the main entrances to Market Street business owners
L. Announcements
  a. Next Meeting Date will be on March 23, 2022 at 7 pm PST
M. Adjournment

FEBRUARY 2022_PTC COMMISSION MEETING AGENDA.DOCX
   CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Parking and Traffic Commission
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  Wednesday, January 26, 2022 at 7:00 p.m.
  JANUARY 2022 MEETING MINUTES

1. Roll Call
A. A meeting was held at the City of Inglewood located on the 1st Floor in Conference Room A at
  7:05 pm.
B. Attendees included:
  1. Charles Braggs, District 1
  2. Leonel Garcia, District 2
  3. Brett C.S. Roberts, District 3
  4. Barbara Brooks, District 4
  5. Diana Maximo, Operations Manager
  6. William Thompson, Traffic Operations Manager
  7. Peter Puglese, City of Inglewood Traffic Engineer
  8. Raquel Méndez, City of Inglewood Associate Engineer

2. Approval of Minutes
A. Approval of Minutes for October 27, 2021.
  1. Leonel Garcia, District 2, made a motion to accept the meeting notes.  Seconded by
  Commissioner Brett C.S. Roberts, District 3.
  2. Four of the five members approved the meeting minutes.

3. Public Comments
A. The topic discussed by the public was Citywide Residential Permit Parking Program
  1. A 6th Avenue resident reported lost items during the 2021 holiday seasons to the Parking and
  Traffic Commission and wanted to bring it to the attention of the City.
  2. A Nutwood Street resident mentioned the lack of parking enforcement during the event.
  Additional, the resident received no response when contacting the parking dispatcher. The
  resident would like the city to respond quickly and enforce signs to prevent violations by non-
  residents and protect the safety of residents. The resident even recommended raising the price
  of the citation and increasing parking officers during the days of the event. City staff explained
  to the resident that the City Council is reviewing the citations and will continue to address the
  concern. Additionally, it was added that citations are issued electronically, and 20 to 30
  parking officers are deployed to each event prior to the start of the event.
  3. A 118th Street resident opposed the parking permit program due to lack of fairness, censorship
  of privacy, its scope and cost. It is not a family friendly program. The resident raised concern
  about lack of planning by Sofi Stadium due to not providing sufficient and affordable
  transportation for their Patrons. The resident asked to be removed from the program as District
  11 is not near Sofi Stadium and is not affected. Additionally, the resident inquired about the
  implementation of the signage since the installation has stopped. City staff explained that the

  city is making some changes but signage will be installed. The next area they will be working
  on is around Arbor Vitae Street.
  4. A Crenshaw Boulevard resident shared that non-residents park on the local streets and wait for
  an Uber/Lyft driver to go to the Stadium. No parking officers have been seen at the perimeters.
  The resident also added that the transportation systems that were going to be in place were not
  put in place. Resident requested further enforcement action from the police and parking.
  Residents have done their part by signing up for the Parking Permit Program.
  5. An 8th Avenue resident informed the Commission that parking for Darby Park on Pincay Drive
  is closed to residents during an event. Resident parks on 90th Street/Pincay Drive to enjoy
  Darby Park, but this is not an option for resident during events. City staff will coordinate with
  the traffic operations management team to see how to address these concerns and allow resident
  access to Darby Park.
  6. A 7th Avenue resident petitioned the City to repair the uneven sidewalk seen on most streets,
  on and around 7th Avenue. City staff mentioned that they will bring this issue to the civil
  engineering team to add this street to capital projects.

4. Unfinished Business: None
A. Update on the Request to Amend the Citywide Parking Permit Program on 4th Ave between Arbor
  Vitae St and Hardy St. The petition did not meet the 75% vote requirements for the district's
  amendment. Therefore, no further action is required.

5. New Business
A. Request to Amend the Citywide Parking Permit Program on 7th Ave between Century Blvd. and
  Hardy St
  1. As information, Twenty six (26) valid signatures were submitted for the application. There are
  forty-six (46) homes located between Hardy Street and Century Boulevard on 7th Avenue and
  roughly fifty-seven percent (57%) of all households in the block signed the petition in favor of
  eliminating the permit parking restrictions.
  2. The meeting was attended by residents on 7th Avenue and had the opportunity to support the
  decision to withdraw the program. Some of the reasons given to the commission are as follows.
  a) The residents of Seventh Avenue suggested that the block is not affected by the events at SoFi
  Stadium.
  b) The resident takes two hours to go shopping plus the stress of traffic because of the event.
  c) Residents asked why the city doesn't have a strong parking enforcement like street sweeping
  days.
  d) Another comment was the WOW Billboard placed in the neighborhood creating a distraction.
  Uneven or broken sidewalks, curbs and gutters are not repaired or observed more often.

  e) The resident doesn't want to play musical car in their own home just to fear a citation.
  Residents asked how it was determined to only give residents two tickets.
  f) The program is inconvenient and does not provide any support to residents. This also creates
  more traffic and stress for the resident to handle as normal on a daily basis.
  g) The block has plenty of parking even during events.

  3. As a result, Commissioner Roberts made the first motion to approve the request to begin the
  voting process. All four district commissioners voted to approve. Public Works will follow
  the steps on Amending or Terminating a Permit Parking District described in the Inglewood
  Municipal Code Section 3-76.1.

6. Public Hearing: None
7. Resolution: None
8. Referral from City Council/City Department: None
9. Parking and Traffic Control: None
10.Police Department: None
11.Commissioner Initiatives:
A. Update on the recommendation on District 4's Request for flashing red lights at 117th Street
  1. A study will be conducted to address whether it is possible to install a stop-sign at the
  intersection.
B. District 1's request that a loading / unloading zone be located near main entrances to Market Street
  business owners
  1. 8th Avenue resident and business owner since 2001 on Market Street wants to have a passenger
  loading and unloading zone on Market Street.
  2. City Staff will investigate and provide recommendation. City staff mentioned that a
  loading/unloading zone cannot be implemented for the diagonal parking spot, but 20 minutes
  (green border) may be feasible.

12.Announcements: The next meeting was announced to be on February 23, 2022 at 7 pm PST
13.Adjournment: The meeting was adjourned at 8:40 pm Pacific Time.

  OFFICE OF THE CITY MANAGER
DATE:  February 23rd, 2022
TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission
FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer
SUBJECT:  Request to Amend Citywide Parking Permit Program for 108th Street
  between Spinning Avenue and Wilkie Avenue/6th Avenue

RECOMMENDATION:
It is requested, the Parking and Traffic Commission review the information included in this report,
conduct a public hearing to receive testimony and consider the recommendation of the City
Traffic Engineer as to a possible amendment of the Residential Parking Permit Program for
108th Street between Spinning Avenue and Wilkie Avenue/6th Avenue.

DISCUSSION:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a city-wide residential parking permit program 24 hours
a days/7 days a week with 2 hour parking Monday through Sunday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (Ordinace
No. 20-09). The program was adopted to more effectively and efficiently protect the residential
communities from non-resident vehicle intrusion. The Citywide Permit Parking Program map is
shown in Attachment No. 1.

On September 8th, 2021, Public Works Department received a petition requesting the removal
of permit parking for 108th Street between Spinning Avenue and Wilkie Avenue/6th Avenue.
The petition was filed by Janice Wilson. The request is shown in Attachment No. 2. The Public
Works Department staff received and reviewed the petition. Thirteen (13) valid signatures were
submitted for the application. There are thirty (30) households on 108th Street between Spinning
Avenue and Wilkie Avenue/6th Avenue and approximately forty-three percent (43%) of all
households on the block signed the petition in favor of removing permit parking restrictions as
shown in Attachment No. 3.

We request the Parking and Traffic Commission provide direction to staff on amending the City's
Parking Permit Program for 108th Street between Spinning Avenue and Wilkie Avenue/6th
Avenue by eliminating the parking restriction by:
  (1) Approving the request to begin the voting process or
  (2) Denying the request and terminating the petition process.

Section 3-73. Miscellaneous Vehicles.

  It shall be unlawful for any person to deposit, leave, place, or park in any street any cement or concrete mixer, wheelbarrow, push-
cart, hand-drawn or hand-propelled vehicle or other object, thing or property in such a manner or for such a time as to interfere with
traffic, either vehicular or pedestrian, in or upon such street or in such a manner as to constitute a hazard to the safety of traffic or of
any person or persons or property in and upon such street, or fail to immediately remove the same upon order of any police or traffic
officer of the City; provided, however, that the Public Works Director shall have the right and power to authorize in writing, for limited
periods of time, the placing or parking of any such vehicle, object and/or thing on any street in such manner as will not constitute the
same a nuisance or a hazard to life or property or unreasonably interfere with traffic in or upon such street.
(Ord. 2348 7-31-79; Ord. 96-21 9-24-96)

Section 3-74. Vehicles for Sale. Advertising.

  It shall be unlawful for any person to stand or park a vehicle upon any street for the purpose of displaying such vehicle for sale by
sign or otherwise. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a vehicle privately owned by a person not in the business of selling vehicles may
have displayed on the inside of any side window one “For Sale” sign not exceeding two hundred square inches in size and indicating
thereon the owner’s address and phone number.

Section 3-75. Special District Parking Regulations.

  To protect the public health, welfare, security and peace of persons residing or conducting business in the vicinity of certain major
entertainment, commercial or industrial facilities whose employees and/or patrons can cause traffic congestion, introduce transient
persons and/or adversely reduce the availability of public street parking in the adjacent neighborhood, there exists the need to limit
parking on the street(s) fronting their homes and local businesses to the residents and local business persons who would otherwise lack
adequate parking accommodations for their respective premises. Under such circumstances, a Permit Parking District may be
established for the affected neighborhood limiting on-street parking during specific days and times to those residents and business
persons of the neighborhood who display a parking permit upon their vehicles. A Permit Parking District shall not be established for
the purpose of creating an exclusive parking zone on public streets for the pleasure of local residents when there is no outstanding
evidence of a severe and large-scale shortage of on-street parking and/or related traffic congestion caused by a neighboring facility that
generates such parking demand or traffic congestion on local streets. The City of Inglewood shall maintain standards and regulations
for the establishment and maintenance of a Permit Parking District, for the issuance of parking permits and for the enforcement of
these regulations.
(Ord. 2339 5-22-79; Ord. 88-3 2-9-88; Ord. 90-9 3-20-90; Ord. 99-17 6-1-99; Ord. 02-05 2-5-02)

Section 3-76. Establishment of a Permit Parking District.

  A Permit Parking District may be established in any of the following manners:
  (a) Upon the receipt of a petition from the residents and/or business persons of a particular neighborhood requesting the
establishment of a Permit Parking District and citing the reasons for such request, the Public Works Director or designee shall study
the request and the site of the request to determine if a district is warranted and if there are alternative means to resolve any
neighborhood parking problems that instigated the petition. The Director or designee shall further determine the appropriate boundary
 of any prospective district. The petition must bear the signatures of adults from a minimum of ten different households and/or
businesses as evidence of a neighborhood desire to establish a district.
  The findings of the study and recommendations of the Director or designee shall be presented to the Parking and Traffic
Commission at a public hearing. Both petitioners and owners of those properties fronting on the street(s) that may be included within
the district shall be duly notified of the public hearing. After receiving the recommendation of the Public Works Director and the
comments of the public, the Commission shall determine if the establishment of a Permit Parking District is warranted and what the
boundaries of the district should be. If determined to be warranted by the Commission, the Public Works Director or designee shall
mail or otherwise deliver one questionnaire to each readily known address within the proposed district (properties fronting on any
street or portions of streets that will be subject to permit parking) requesting approval or disapproval of the establishment of the
district. If a minimum of seventy-five percent of the questionnaires returned to the Public Works Director, within a minimum period of
thirty calendar days, support the establishment of the district, an ordinance establishing the Permit Parking District shall be submitted
to the City Council for consideration and adoption to amend the Municipal Code accordingly.
  (b) City staff may recommend the establishment of a Permit Parking District to the City Council and introduce an ordinance for
the City Council’s consideration.
  (c) The City Council may, at its discretion, direct City staff to study the establishment of a Permit Parking District and introduce
an ordinance for the City Council’s consideration.
(Ord. 2297 3-7-78; Ord. 2339 5-22-79; Ord. 88-3 2-9-88; Ord. 90-9 3-20-90; Ord. 99-17 6-1-99; Ord. 02-05 2-5-02; Ord. 07-04 3-
6-07; Ord. 20-09 6-16-20)

Section 3-76.1. Amending or Terminating a Permit Parking District.

  The procedures by which an existing Permit Parking District can be amended or terminated shall be pursuant to any of the
procedures set forth in Section 3-76 of this Article.
(Ord. 07-04 3-6-07; Ord. 20-09 6-16-20)

Section 3-77. Posting Requirements.

  The City shall not enforce any Permit Parking District prohibition or restriction unless signs or markings giving adequate notice
have been placed in accordance with Vehicle Code Section 22507. It shall be the duty of the Public Works Director to cause such signs
or markings to be placed.
(Ord. 02-05 2-5-02; Ord. 20-09 6-16-20)

Section 3-78. Permit Issuance and Use Procedure.

  (a) Applications for Parking Permits. Applicants for a parking permit shall be required to present such proof as is required by the
City, including, but not limited to, proof of residence, employment, or ownership of a business in the Permit Parking District for which
a parking permit is sought; ownership of the vehicle, license plate number, and proof of current registration. An application for a
renewal of a parking permit shall conform to the requirements of this Section.
  (b) Types of Permits and Fees. City staff shall prepare a chart specifying the various types of parking permits the City may issue,
including, but not limited to, residential, business, or guest permits; daily, monthly, or annual permits; the maximum number of permits
that may be issued to each residence or business, by type of parking permit; the fees for each type of parking permit; and any other
rules governing the use of the parking permits. The chart shall be presented to the City Council for adoption by resolution and the
parking permit fees shall be made part of the Master Fee Schedule.
  A residence or business applicant shall have a street address located in the Parking Permit District for which a permit is sought. An
applicant whose residence or business is located on a street that is the border of two or more Permit Parking Districts may be issued a
permit to park a vehicle on either side of the bordering street.
  (c) Full Payment of Fees. All parking permit applications shall include full payment of the parking permit fee. Furthermore, no
parking permit shall be issued to any applicant until the applicant has paid all outstanding parking citations, including any civil
penalties and related fees.
   (d) Issuance and Use of Permit. A parking permit may be issued and enforced using either a virtual or physical permit. A virtual
permit shall be issued to the license plate number of the applicant’s registered vehicle and enforced through an Automated License
Plate Reader System (ALPRS). Each virtual permit holder shall be responsible for ensuring that their license plate is capable of being
read by the ALPRS.
  The City may issue a physical permit, such as a sticker or hanging tag, to the applicant. The holder of a physical permit shall be
responsible for making sure that the physical permit is displayed in accordance with the City’s rules so as to be clearly visible from
outside of the vehicle.
  A parking permit is valid only for parking in the specified Permit Parking District and it does not guarantee the availability of a
parking space. The parking permit holder shall be subject to each and every condition and restriction set forth in this Chapter and as
provided for the Permit Parking District for which it was issued. The issuance of a parking permit does not exempt the holder from
compliance with any other parking regulation, including, but not limited to, vehicle type, height or weight restrictions; zones that
prohibit the stopping, parking or standing of vehicles; and street sweeping parking restrictions.
  (e) Revocation of Parking Permit. A parking permit holder shall not sell, rent or otherwise transfer a parking permit to another
person, unless authorized by the City, or present false or fraudulent information to obtain a parking permit. A parking permit may not
be altered or reproduced. A violation of any City rule regulating the application for or use of parking permits may result in the
revocation of the parking permit, the revocation of any other permits issued to the permittee, and the disqualification of the permittee
from being issued any future parking permit.
  (f) Replacement of Permit. A permittee seeking replacement of a lost or stolen permit shall pay a replacement permit fee as
established by City Council resolution and set forth in the Master Fee Schedule.
(Ord. 14-09 7-22-14; Ord. 19-05 1-8-19; Ord. 20-09 6-16-20)

Section 3-79. Exemptions from Permit Parking District Prohibitions.

  Only the following vehicles shall be exempt from enforcement of the Permit Parking District prohibitions in Section 3-80:
  (a)  Any vehicle displaying a valid parking permit.
  (b)  Any licensed physician’s vehicle parked while making a professional call.
  (c)  Any vehicle parked in an individual curbside parking space governed by a parking meter.
  (d) Any vehicle parked in an individual curbside parking space that is specifically exempt by a posted sign or marking, so long as
said vehicle is in compliance with all other parking conditions or limitations specified on the sign or marking.
  (e) Any vehicle exempt under any other applicable law, including, but not limited to, Municipal Code Sections 3-65(c), 3-65.1(b),
3-65.2(c), and 3-80(b).
(Ord. 92-6 6-9-92; Ord. 99-1 1-26-99; Ord. 02-05 2-5-02; Ord. 20-09 6-16-20)

Section 3-80. Permit Parking District Restrictions—Tow Away Authorized.

  Upon designation of a Permit Parking District, the Public Works Director shall determine whether permit parking restrictions apply
twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week (24/7), or any portion thereof, based upon the needs of the Permit Parking District, and
cause appropriate signs or markings to be placed indicating prominently thereon, the parking limitation, period of the day for its
application, and the fact that vehicles with valid permits shall be exempt therefrom. Unless an exemption in Section 3-79 applies, it is
unlawful for a person to park a vehicle on a City street located on or in Permit Parking District, at any time, without displaying a valid
parking permit.
  As authorized by Vehicle Code Section 22651(n), the City may cause to be removed any vehicle parked in violation of this Section,
and the registered owner thereof shall be responsible for paying the impoundment and storage fees established by the City. It shall be
the duty of the Public Works Director to identify areas where signs giving notice of removal for a violation of this Section shall be
placed and cause such signs to be placed. No vehicle shall be removed for a violation of this section unless signs giving notice of
removal have been placed in accordance with Vehicle Code Section 22651(n) and Municipal Code Section 3-58.
(Ord. 1961 9-13-68; Ord. 02-05 2-5-02; Ord. 06-08 6-20-06; Ord. 09-23 12-15-09; Ord. 10-11 6-22-10; Ord. 14-09 7-22-14; Ord.
15-09 2-3-15; Ord. 15-20 9-1-15; Ord. 17-10 7-11-17; Ord. 17-12 8-1-17; Ord. 17-13 8-1-17; Ord. 17-17 9-19-17; Ord. 20-09 6-
16-20)
 Section 3-81. Parking District Boundaries Defined.

  The boundaries of each Permit Parking District are defined by the Permit Parking Districts map presented to the City Council for
adoption as part of Ordinance No. 20-09. All City streets located on or within the boundaries of a Permit Parking District shall be
subject to the permit parking prohibitions or restrictions of that District only when appropriate signs or markings giving adequate
notice have been placed.

  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Elimination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the amendment
of a residential Permit Parking District on 108th Street between Spinning Avenue and Wilkie Avenue/6th
Avenue. Per Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to
the Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday February 23rd, 2022 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses fronting the subject street. Any interested person may
attend this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the specific areas listed above an
opportunity to state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of a Permit Parking District is to assure the availability to residents of some on-street
(curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a nearby
commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-
street parking on 108th Street between Spinning Avenue and Wilkie Avenue/6th Avenue is severely
impacted in this manner and if the elimination of a Permit Parking District would be warranted. If it is
determined to be warranted, ballots will be mailed to each household within the proposed parking
district. A 75-percent (75 %) approval is required to eliminate a Permit Parking District.

If a Permit Parking District is eliminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will not be
restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events.

If you have any questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend
the public hearing, please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

  AVISO DE AUDIENCIA PÚBLICA
  Petición de Eliminación del Permiso de
  Estacionamiento en la Zona Residencial
Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la
enmiendacion de un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial en 108th Street entre
Spinning Avenue y Wilkie Avenue/6th Avenue. De acuerdo con las Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código
Municipal de Inglewood, este asunto se presentará a la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de
Inglewood a la hora y lugar especificados:

  Miércoles 23 de Febrero de 2022 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones que se encuentran al frente de la calle en
cuestión. Cualquier persona interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es brindar a todos los residentes de las áreas específicas
enumeradas anteriormente la oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema. El propósito de un
Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso es asegurar la disponibilidad para los residentes de algunos
espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (en la acera) dentro de un vecindario donde los clientes y / o
empleados de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana usen todo los espacios de
estacionamiento disponible en la calle

Por lo tanto, la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood considerará si la disponibilidad
de estacionamiento en la calle en la 108th Street entre Spinning Avenue y Wilkie Avenue/6th Avenue
se ve gravemente afectada de esta manera y si se justificaría la eliminación de un Distrito de
Estacionamiento con Permiso. Si se determina que se justifica, las boletas se enviarán por correo a
cada hogar dentro del distrito de estacionamiento propuesto. Se requiere una aprobación del 75 por
ciento (75%) para eliminar un distrito de estacionamiento con permiso.

Si se elimina un distrito de estacionamiento con permiso, no se restringirá el estacionamiento en las
calles públicas a todos los residentes y visitantes de este vecindario en ningún momento; incluso
durante los eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea expresar una
opinión pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento de Obras
Públicas de Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.
